references.text: Shortly before this verse, John the Baptist says that he baptizes with water and points out that there is one standing among them whom they do not know ([ref:Joh 1:26|John 1:26]). This is the immediate context for his testimony that the purpose of water baptism was to reveal the Messiah to Israel.

John expands on his testimony: He who sent him to baptize with water said that the one he sees the Spirit descending and remaining on is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit ([ref:Joh 1:33|John 1:33]). This confirms that water baptism was a means to reveal Jesus.

Immediately after the source verse, John the Baptist summarizes his testimony: "I have seen it, and I have testified that he is the Son of God" ([ref:Joh 1:34|John 1:34]). This is the direct conclusion of the mission he describes in verse 31 – to reveal the Messiah to Israel.

Already in the prologue it is stated that John came to testify about the light, so that all might believe through him ([ref:Joh 1:7|John 1:7]). His baptism in water was precisely part of this testimony mission – to make Jesus known to Israel.
Also in Matthew's Gospel, John the Baptist testifies about his water baptism in contrast to the one who comes after him, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire ([ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11]).
Mark also tells of John the Baptist's preaching where he contrasts his water baptism with the coming one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit ([ref:Mark 1:7-8|Mark 1:7-8]).

Luke reports on John's baptism in water and his pointing testimony toward the coming Messiah ([ref:Luk 3:16|Luke 3:16]), which aligns with John's words that the purpose of water baptism was to reveal Christ to Israel.

Paul explains in Ephesus that John's baptism was a baptism of repentance, and that John told the people to believe in the one who comes after him, namely Jesus ([ref:Apg 19:4|Acts 19:4]). This confirms that the baptism had as its purpose to point toward and reveal Christ.

The prophecy about a voice crying out in the wilderness to prepare the way for the Lord ([ref:Jes 40:3|Isaiah 40:3]) forms the prophetic foundation for John the Baptist's mission, which he describes here: to reveal the Messiah to Israel.

The prophet Malachi predicts that God will send his messenger to prepare the way ([ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1]). John the Baptist's mission of baptizing in water to reveal Christ to Israel is the fulfillment of this prophecy.
